references.desc: Monetary theory, critique of the gold standard, The Economic Consequences of the Peace on Versailles reparations

references.name: Milton Friedman
references.desc: Monetarist analysis of the Great Depression—the Fed’s failure to provide sufficient liquidity

references.name: Ben Bernanke
references.desc: Depression scholar turned Fed Chairman who applied historical lessons to 2008 crisis response

references.name: Hank Paulson
references.desc: Treasury Secretary during 2008—bold CEO-style decision-making, architect of TARP and GSE conservatorship

references.name: Tim Geithner
references.desc: NY Fed President then Treasury Secretary—pragmatic operator who designed stress tests and coordinated bank recapitalization

references.name: Herbert Hoover
references.desc: President whose austerity policies (Revenue Act of 1932) deepened the Great Depression

references.name: Franklin Roosevelt
references.desc: Ended the depression “on a dime” by delinking from gold, providing bank liquidity, and launching massive fiscal stimulus

references.name: Rudolf Havenstein
references.desc: Reichsbank president who presided over Weimar hyperinflation—printed money to fund reparations in foreign currency

references.name: Gustav Stresemann
references.desc: German Chancellor who stabilized the currency through the Rentenmark and Dawes Plan

references.name: Larry Summers
references.desc: Compared crisis policy to battlefield medicine; exposed Fannie/Freddie’s political power

references.name: Constantino Bresciani-Turroni
references.desc: The Economics of Inflation (1937)—foundational study of Weimar hyperinflation

references.name: Barry Eichengreen
references.desc: Hall of Mirrors (2016)—comparing the Great Depression and Great Recession
